title: Liberal senator Leah Blyth announces defection to One Nation
summary: South Australian senator labels One Nation the ‘only party with the bold ideas needed to turn this country around’

blocks.text: Leah Blyth, federal Liberal senator for South Australia, has announced she is defecting to One Nation, becoming the party’s first upper-house member for the state.
Blyth, a member of Angus Taylor’s shadow cabinet, said she did not believe the Coalition was capable of opposing the Albanese government, which was “running the country into the ground”.
“I can no longer in good conscience tell Australians that the Liberal Party can save this country,” she said in a statement.
“Australia is a country worth fighting for … I want our children to grow up proud of their country, with the freedom and opportunity to build a better life.
“One Nation has never shied away from confronting the uncomfortable truths facing our nation. They are the only party with the bold ideas needed to turn this country around.”
Pauline Hanson welcomed the South Australian senator, and said she would “build on One Nation’s expanding support within the state”.
Hanson posted a video to social media on Wednesday night, cooking a steak in a sandwich press and asked viewers to “guess who this is for”.
It was a reference back to the same meal shared between the One Nation leader and then-Nationals MP Barnaby Joyce ahead of his defection.
On Thursday morning, Nationals leader Matt Canavan called Blyth’s defection “disappointing on a number of levels” and condemned the move as part of a broader pattern of behaviour from One Nation.
The deputy Liberal leader, Jane Hume, similarly described the move as a “disappointing decision” but said Blyth “wasn’t a big contributor to the party room”.
Speaking to Radio National, Canavan said the move took him by surprise.
“I try and be friends with everyone … and I thought I was friends with Leah, but there was no warning from her.”
Speaking to Blyth’s reasoning that her values aligned closer to One Nation, Cavanan said the move “smacks of self-interest to me”.
“Good luck to her. Leah went to the election last year supporting net zero. She didn’t oppose the hate speech laws earlier this year, like we did - the Nationals.
“To turn around now a few months later and say, ‘my principles and policies are more aligned with One Nation’ – I mean, give me a break.”
